subproblems.title: Support lemma (Simon 6.2.11): a current vanishes on test forms supported away from its support
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set, S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n) with tsupport ω disjoint from spt S, where spt S = U ∖ Z_S and Z_S is the union of all open W with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and S(η) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W (GeometricCurrentOn.support). Then S(ω) = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.11 (definition of spt T, chapter-06.txt lines 297–301); the partition-of-unity argument below is the standard reason why the union in 2.11 is itself a set on which the current vanishes. Notation: "S vanishes on W" means S(η) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W.
1. K := tsupport ω is compact and K ⊆ U, because ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) is a compactly supported smooth form with tsupport ω ⊆ U. If K = ∅ then ω = 0 and S(ω) = 0 by linearity; assume K ≠ ∅.
2. Since K ⊆ U and K ∩ spt S = ∅, we have K ⊆ U ∖ spt S ⊆ Z_S. By compactness there are finitely many open sets W₁,…,W_m from the family defining Z_S (each with S vanishing on W_i) such that K ⊆ W₁ ∪ … ∪ W_m.
3. Take a smooth partition of unity on ℝ^P subordinate to the open cover {W₁,…,W_m, ℝ^P ∖ K} (e.g. Mathlib's SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate for the closed set K and the cover by W₁,…,W_m): smooth ψ₁,…,ψ_m : ℝ^P → [0,1] with tsupport ψ_i ⊆ W_i for each i and Σ_i ψ_i(y) = 1 for every y ∈ K.
4. For each i, ψ_iω (pointwise product of a smooth function and a smooth n-form) is smooth, and tsupport(ψ_iω) ⊆ tsupport ψ_i ∩ tsupport ω ⊆ W_i ∩ K; in particular it is compact and contained in U. Thus ψ_iω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport(ψ_iω) ⊆ W_i, and S(ψ_iω) = 0 since S vanishes on W_i.
5. ω = Σ_i ψ_iω pointwise: if ω(y) ≠ 0 then y ∈ K and Σ_iψ_i(y) = 1; if ω(y) = 0 both sides vanish. By linearity of S, S(ω) = Σ_i S(ψ_iω) = 0.
proof_key_steps: tsupport ω is a compact subset of the zero region of S, hence covered by finitely many open sets on which S vanishes.
A smooth partition of unity subordinate to this finite cover splits ω into test forms supported in those sets.
Each piece is annihilated by S; linearity gives S(ω) = 0.

subproblems.title: Mass on open sets of an integer multiplicity current equals its representation measure (Simon Ch. 6, 3.2(3))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and U ⊆ ℝ^P open. Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity representation in U (contract IMRep U n): M ⊆ U Borel and countably n-rectifiable; θ : ℝ^P → ℕ Borel with θ ≥ 1 on M and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U; ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) (continuous linear functionals on n-covectors) a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M, such that for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M there is an orthonormal family τ_1, …, τ_n spanning an approximate tangent space of M at x with ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ = α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all α, or ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ = −α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all α. Here Hⁿ = μHE[n]. Let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be represented by R: T(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Put μ_R(A) := ∫_{M∩A} θ dHⁿ (the contract's R.measure). Then for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, M_W(T) = μ_R(W), where M_W(T) := sup{max(T(ω), 0) : ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x} ∈ [0, ∞] (SimonGMT massOn) and |α| := (Σ_{1≤i_1<⋯<i_n≤P} α(e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n})²)^{1/2} is the Euclidean coefficient norm of n-covectors (Simon 6.1.15, 6.2.5).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = R.measure W
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 763–768), stated there without proof; the argument is the one indicated in Remark 2.6 (properties (a), (b) of the norm) together with 2.7–2.8 (lines 243–283). Write E for the space of n-covectors on ℝ^P with the inner product ⟨α, α'⟩_E := Σ_I α(e_I) α'(e_I) (sum over increasing n-tuples I = (i_1 < ⋯ < i_n), e_I := (e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n})); its norm is |·|. If n > P then E = 0, every n-form vanishes, so T = 0 and M_W(T) = 0, and Hⁿ = 0 on ℝ^P (Hausdorff dimension P < n), so μ_R = 0 and the claim holds. Assume n ≤ P.
1. (Algebra.) Let τ_1, …, τ_n ∈ ℝ^P be orthonormal and let A be the n×P matrix A_{ik} := ⟨τ_i, e_k⟩. Expanding each τ_i in the standard basis, multilinearity and the alternating property give α(τ_1, …, τ_n) = Σ_I det(A_I) α(e_I), where A_I is the n×n submatrix of A with columns I. By Cauchy–Schwarz, |α(τ)| ≤ |α| (Σ_I det(A_I)²)^{1/2}, and by the Cauchy–Binet formula Σ_I det(A_I)² = det(AAᵀ) = det(⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) = 1. Hence |α(τ_1, …, τ_n)| ≤ |α| for every α ∈ E. The covector α_τ(v_1, …, v_n) := det(⟨τ_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j} satisfies α_τ(e_I) = det(A_I); hence ⟨α, α_τ⟩_E = α(τ) for every α, |α_τ| = 1 and α_τ(τ) = 1. (For n = 0 everything is trivial: α(τ) = α(∅) and |α| = |α(∅)|.)
2. (Consequences on M.) Let J : E* → E be the Riesz isomorphism (⟨α, J(η)⟩_E = η(α)) and β := J ∘ ξ, an Hⁿ⌞M-measurable E-valued map. For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M we have ξ(x) = ±(α ↦ α(τ)) with τ orthonormal, so by step 1: |⟨α, ξ(x)⟩| ≤ |α| for every α ∈ E, β(x) = ±α_τ, |β(x)| = 1 and ⟨β(x), ξ(x)⟩ = 1.
3. (Integrability.) For every compact K ⊆ U, μ_R(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞. If ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), then tsupport ω is a compact subset of U and |θ⟨ω, ξ⟩| ≤ (sup|ω|)·θ·1_{tsupport ω} Hⁿ-a.e. on M, so the integrand is integrable and T(ω) = ∫ ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R.
4. (Upper bound.) Let ω be admissible: ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω| ≤ 1. For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ 1, and ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ = 0 if x ∉ W. Hence T(ω) ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ = μ_R(W), so max(T(ω), 0) ≤ μ_R(W). Taking the supremum, M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W).
5. (Lower bound: reduction to compact sets.) V := U ∩ W is open and μ_R(W) = μ_R(V) since M ⊆ U. V is the increasing union of the compact sets K_i := {x ∈ V : |x| ≤ i, dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ V) ≥ 1/i} (K_i := {|x| ≤ i} if V = ℝ^P), so μ_R(V) = sup_i μ_R(K_i). It therefore suffices to prove M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(K) − 4η for every compact K ⊆ V and every η > 0. Fix K and η; if μ_R(K) = 0 there is nothing to prove.
6. (Open neighbourhood.) Choose δ > 0 with {x : dist(x, K) ≤ 2δ} ⊆ V. The sets O_s := {x : dist(x, K) < s}, 0 < s ≤ δ, have compact closures contained in V ⊆ U, so μ_R(O_δ) < ∞ and μ_R(O_s) ↓ μ_R(K) as s ↓ 0 (continuity from above; K is closed). Fix s ∈ (0, δ] with μ_R(O ∖ K) < η, where O := O_s.
7. (Lusin.) μ_R⌞K is a finite Borel measure on a compact metric space and β is μ_R-measurable; by Lusin's theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17; SimonGMT Chapter01/Lusin.lean) there is a compact K' ⊆ K with μ_R(K ∖ K') < η such that β|K' is continuous; by inner regularity we may also assume that |β| = 1 and ⟨β, ξ⟩ = 1 at every point of K' (these hold μ_R-a.e. by step 2).
8. (Continuous extension.) By Tietze's extension theorem (applied to the coordinates of β in a basis of E), β|K' extends to a continuous g_0 : ℝ^P → E. Let r : E → E be the radial retraction r(α) := α if |α| ≤ 1, r(α) := α/|α| otherwise (continuous, |r| ≤ 1, r = id on the closed unit ball). By Urysohn's lemma choose a continuous χ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with χ = 1 on K' and tsupport χ ⊆ O compact. Put g := χ·(r ∘ g_0). Then g is continuous, tsupport g ⊆ O is compact, |g| ≤ 1 everywhere, and g = β on K'.
9. (Smoothing.) Let φ_σ (σ > 0) be a standard mollifier (smooth, ≥ 0, ∫φ_σ = 1, supported in the closed σ-ball) and g_σ := g * φ_σ (componentwise convolution). Then g_σ is C^∞, tsupport g_σ ⊆ {x : dist(x, tsupport g) ≤ σ} ⊆ O for 0 < σ < dist(tsupport g, ℝ^P ∖ O), |g_σ(x)| ≤ ∫ |g(x − y)| φ_σ(y) dy ≤ 1 (convexity of the norm), and g_σ → g uniformly as σ ↓ 0 (g is uniformly continuous). Viewed as an n-form, g_σ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (compact support in O ⊆ U) and g_σ is admissible for M_W(T) (O ⊆ V ⊆ W, |g_σ| ≤ 1).
10. (Estimate.) By steps 2–3, |T(g_σ) − ∫⟨g, ξ⟩ dμ_R| ≤ sup|g_σ − g|·μ_R(closure O) → 0 as σ ↓ 0. On K', ⟨g, ξ⟩ = ⟨β, ξ⟩ = 1; on O ∖ K', ⟨g, ξ⟩ ≥ −|g| ≥ −1 μ_R-a.e.; off O, g = 0. Hence ∫⟨g, ξ⟩ dμ_R ≥ μ_R(K') − μ_R(O ∖ K') ≥ (μ_R(K) − η) − (μ_R(O ∖ K) + μ_R(K ∖ K')) ≥ μ_R(K) − 3η. Therefore max(T(g_σ), 0) ≥ μ_R(K) − 4η for σ small, and M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(K) − 4η.
11. By step 5, M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(W) (also when μ_R(W) = ∞); together with step 4, M_W(T) = μ_R(W). ∎
Remark (reuse; not a proof step). Step 4 proves M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W) and steps 5–11 prove μ_R(W) ≤ M_W(T) for open W. The comparator-accepted DAG declarations dor_ims_massOn_le_measure, of frozen type ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), R.Represents T → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), T.massOn W ≤ R.measure W, and dor_ims_measure_le_massOn, of frozen type ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → R.measure W ≤ T.massOn W, state these two inequalities (the first even without openness of U and W), so a decomposition of this child may reuse them verbatim and conclude by antisymmetry.
proof_key_steps: Cauchy–Binet: for a unit simple n-vector ξ, |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α| (Euclidean coefficient norm), with equality for the dual covector β = J∘ξ, |β| = 1.
Upper bound: T(ω) ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ for admissible ω, so M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W).
Lower bound: inner regularity reduces to compact K ⊆ U ∩ W; Lusin, Tietze, radial truncation, a cut-off and mollification give smooth admissible forms g_σ with T(g_σ) ≥ μ_R(K) − 4η.

subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (K W W' : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → IsIntegerMultiplicity S → IsIntegerMultiplicity T → IsCompact K → (S - T).support ⊆ K → IsOpen W → IsOpen W' → K ⊆ W → W ⊆ W' → CompactlyContained W' U → T.massOn W ≤ S.massOn W → T.massOn W' ≤ S.massOn W'
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 8 of the parent proof, which supplies the details behind Simon's remark after (8) (chapter-07.txt lines 226–229: “In view of the arbitrariness of K, X this will evidently establish the fact that T is minimizing in U”).
1. Let R_S, R_T be IM representations of S and T and μ_S := R_S.measure, μ_T := R_T.measure. By the sibling lemma mass_equals_rep_measure, M_G(S) = μ_S(G) and M_G(T) = μ_T(G) for every open G ⊆ ℝ^P. Both measures vanish outside U and are finite on compact subsets of U (local integrability of the multiplicities).
2. O := U ∖ K is open (K is compact, hence closed). Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ O. Then tsupport ω ∩ spt(S − T) ⊆ O ∩ K = ∅, so (S − T)(ω) = 0 by the sibling lemma vanish_off_support; that is, S(ω) = T(ω).
3. Hence, for every open G ⊆ O, the admissible forms for M_G(S) and for M_G(T) are the same test forms (in 𝒟ⁿ(U), supported in G, of norm ≤ 1) and give the same values, so M_G(S) = M_G(T), i.e. μ_S(G) = μ_T(G) by step 1.
4. Let O_i := {x ∈ O : |x| < i, dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ O) > 1/i} (O_i := {|x| < i} if O = ℝ^P); these are open, increase to O, and have compact closures contained in O ⊆ U, so μ_S(O_i), μ_T(O_i) < ∞. For each i, the finite Borel measures μ_S⌞O_i and μ_T⌞O_i agree on every open set G ⊆ ℝ^P (G ∩ O_i is an open subset of O; step 3), in particular on ℝ^P; the open sets form a π-system generating the Borel σ-algebra, so μ_S⌞O_i = μ_T⌞O_i (uniqueness of finite measures, e.g. Mathlib ext_of_generate_finite). For a Borel set A ⊆ O, continuity from below along O_i ↑ O gives μ_S(A) = lim_i μ_S(A ∩ O_i) = lim_i μ_T(A ∩ O_i) = μ_T(A).
5. W' ∖ W is a Borel set contained in O (W' ⊆ closure(W') ⊆ U and K ⊆ W), so μ_S(W' ∖ W) = μ_T(W' ∖ W).
6. Since W ⊆ W', μ_T(W') = μ_T(W) + μ_T(W' ∖ W) ≤ μ_S(W) + μ_S(W' ∖ W) = μ_S(W'), using μ_T(W) = M_W(T) ≤ M_W(S) = μ_S(W). By step 1, M_{W'}(T) = μ_T(W') ≤ μ_S(W') = M_{W'}(S). ∎
proof_key_steps: By mass_equals_rep_measure, masses on open sets are the representation measures μ_S, μ_T.
By vanish_off_support, S and T agree on test forms supported in O = U ∖ K, so μ_S = μ_T on open subsets of O and hence (finite-measure uniqueness along an exhaustion of O) on all Borel subsets of O.
μ_T(W') = μ_T(W) + μ_T(W' ∖ W) ≤ μ_S(W) + μ_S(W' ∖ W) = μ_S(W').

subproblems.title: Convergence of integrals from limsup on compact sets and liminf on open sets
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set, and μ, μ_j (j ∈ ℕ) Borel measures on ℝ^P such that (a) μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U; (b) limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) for every compact K ⊆ U; (c) μ(G) ≤ liminf_j μ_j(G) for every open G ⊆ U (lim sup and lim inf in [0, ∞]). Then ∫ f dμ_j → ∫ f dμ (Bochner integrals) for every continuous f : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support and tsupport f ⊆ U.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (μs : ℕ → Measure (Euclid P)) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K < ∞) → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → limsup (fun j => μs j K) atTop ≤ μ K) → (∀ G : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen G → G ⊆ U → μ G ≤ liminf (fun j => μs j G) atTop) → ∀ f : Euclid P → ℝ, Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → tsupport f ⊆ U → Tendsto (fun j => ∫ x, f x ∂(μs j)) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, f x ∂μ))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the last sentence of Simon's proof of 7.2.4 (chapter-07.txt lines 284–289: from (13), (14) “it now easily follows (by a standard approximation argument) that ∫ f dμ_{T_j} → ∫ f dμ_T”); step 9 of the parent proof. Details:
1. Let C := tsupport f, a compact subset of U. By (a), μ(C) < ∞; by (b), limsup_j μ_j(C) ≤ μ(C) < ∞, so there are j₀ ∈ ℕ and Λ < ∞ with μ_j(C) ≤ Λ for all j ≥ j₀. Every bounded Borel function vanishing outside C is integrable for μ and for every μ_j with j ≥ j₀. Since convergence of a sequence depends only on its tail, only j ≥ j₀ is considered below.
2. Write f = f⁺ − f⁻ with f^± := max(±f, 0): continuous, nonnegative, vanishing outside C, and ∫ f dν = ∫ f⁺ dν − ∫ f⁻ dν for ν ∈ {μ} ∪ {μ_j : j ≥ j₀}. So it suffices to prove ∫ g dμ_j → ∫ g dμ for a continuous g ≥ 0 vanishing outside C. Let b := max g; if b = 0 both sides vanish.
3. (Layer cake.) For ν as above, ∫ g dν = ∫_0^b ν({g > t}) dt (Cavalieri's principle, e.g. Mathlib Integrable.integral_eq_integral_meas_lt); the integrand is ≤ ν(C) < ∞ and vanishes for t ≥ b.
4. Fix t > 0. G_t := {g > t} is open and G_t ⊆ C ⊆ U; K_t := {g ≥ t} is closed and contained in C, hence compact and contained in U. The sets {g = t}, t > 0, are pairwise disjoint subsets of C and μ(C) < ∞, so D := {t > 0 : μ({g = t}) > 0} is countable. For t ∈ (0, b) ∖ D we have μ(K_t) = μ(G_t), and by (b) and (c), limsup_j μ_j(G_t) ≤ limsup_j μ_j(K_t) ≤ μ(K_t) = μ(G_t) ≤ liminf_j μ_j(G_t). Hence μ_j(G_t) → μ(G_t) for L¹-a.e. t ∈ (0, b).
5. For j ≥ j₀ and t ∈ (0, b), 0 ≤ μ_j(G_t) ≤ μ_j(C) ≤ Λ, a constant, integrable on (0, b). By dominated convergence and step 3, ∫ g dμ_j = ∫_0^b μ_j(G_t) dt → ∫_0^b μ(G_t) dt = ∫ g dμ.
6. Applying step 5 to g = f⁺ and to g = f⁻ and subtracting gives ∫ f dμ_j → ∫ f dμ. ∎
proof_key_steps: Eventual finiteness: μ_j(spt f) ≤ Λ for large j and μ(spt f) < ∞; reduce to f ≥ 0 via f = f⁺ − f⁻.
Layer cake: ∫ g dν = ∫_0^b ν({g > t}) dt.
For all but countably many t, the open set {g > t} and the compact set {g ≥ t} have the same μ-measure, so (b), (c) give μ_j({g > t}) → μ({g > t}); conclude by dominated convergence.

subproblems.title: Lower semicontinuity of local mass under weak convergence on exhausting domains, along every subsequence (Simon 6.2.14 as used in 7.2.4)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. For j ∈ ℕ let U_j ⊆ ℝ^P be any sets and S_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U_j), and let C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P). Assume (1) for every r ∈ ℝ, closedBall(0, r) ⊆ U_j for all sufficiently large j, and (2) S_j ⇀ C in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly). Then for every strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and every set O ⊆ ℝ^P, M_O(C) ≤ liminf_{i→∞} M_O(S_{φ(i)}) in [0, ∞]. Notation: 𝒟_n(V) = GeometricCurrentOn V n; 𝒟ⁿ(V) = TestFormOn V n (smooth compactly supported n-forms ω on ℝ^P with tsupport ω ⊆ V); for Y ∈ 𝒟_n(V) and any O ⊆ ℝ^P, M_O(Y) := Y.massOn O = sup{ofReal(Y(ω)) : ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V), tsupport ω ⊆ O, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x} ∈ [0, ∞] (SimonGMT massOn, |·| the Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors); currentEval(Y, ω) := Y(ω) if ω is a test form with tsupport ω ⊆ V and 0 otherwise; S_j ⇀ C (ConvergesWeakly Ss C) means currentEval(S_j, ω) → C(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P); thickening(ε, K) = {x : inf_{y∈K} |x − y| < ε}.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Us : ℕ → Set (Euclid P)) (Ss : (j : ℕ) → GeometricCurrentOn (Us j) n) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), (∀ R : ℝ, ∀ᶠ j in atTop, closedBall (0 : Euclid P) R ⊆ Us j) → ConvergesWeakly Ss C → ∀ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ → ∀ O : Set (Euclid P), C.massOn O ≤ liminf (fun i => (Ss (φ i)).massOn O) atTop
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.14 (chapter-06.txt lines 313–316: M_W(T) ≤ liminf_q M_W(T_q) under weak convergence), as invoked in the proof of 7.2.4 for (8) and (14) (chapter-07.txt lines 262–263 and 281–283). This is step (L3) of the parent proof, for currents on the varying domains U_j. The parent states (L3) for bounded open O, but its argument only uses that tsupport ω ⊆ U_j for large j, which already follows from the compactness of tsupport ω; hence the claim holds for every set O.
1. By definition M_O(C) is the supremum in [0, ∞] of ofReal(C(ω)) over the set A := massAdmissibleOn(ℝ^P, n, O) of ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ O and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. So it suffices to show ofReal(C(ω)) ≤ L := liminf_i M_O(S_{φ(i)}) for every ω ∈ A (a supremum of values each ≤ L is ≤ L).
2. Fix ω ∈ A. Being a test form, ω has compact support, so tsupport ω is compact, hence bounded: tsupport ω ⊆ closedBall(0, r) for some r ∈ ℝ.
3. By (1) there is j₀ with closedBall(0, r) ⊆ U_j for all j ≥ j₀. As φ is strictly increasing, φ(i) ≥ i for every i (so φ(i) → ∞), hence closedBall(0, r) ⊆ U_{φ(i)} and therefore tsupport ω ⊆ U_{φ(i)} for all i ≥ j₀.
4. Let i ≥ j₀. Since ω is a test form with tsupport ω ⊆ U_{φ(i)}, the definition of currentEval gives currentEval(S_{φ(i)}, ω) = S_{φ(i)}(ω_i), where ω_i ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U_{φ(i)}) is the same form ω regarded as a test form in U_{φ(i)}. Since tsupport ω_i = tsupport ω ⊆ O and |ω_i(x)| = |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, ω_i ∈ massAdmissibleOn(U_{φ(i)}, n, O), so ofReal(currentEval(S_{φ(i)}, ω)) = ofReal(S_{φ(i)}(ω_i)) ≤ M_O(S_{φ(i)}) (each admissible value is at most the supremum).
5. By (2), currentEval(S_j, ω) → C(ω) as j → ∞; since φ(i) → ∞, also currentEval(S_{φ(i)}, ω) → C(ω) as i → ∞, and by continuity of ofReal : ℝ → [0, ∞], a_i := ofReal(currentEval(S_{φ(i)}, ω)) → ofReal(C(ω)). The liminf of a convergent sequence in [0, ∞] is its limit, so ofReal(C(ω)) = liminf_i a_i.
6. By step 4, a_i ≤ M_O(S_{φ(i)}) for all i ≥ j₀; the liminf is monotone under eventual inequalities (in the complete lattice [0, ∞] no boundedness side conditions arise), so liminf_i a_i ≤ L, i.e. ofReal(C(ω)) ≤ L by step 5.
7. As ω ∈ A was arbitrary, step 1 gives M_O(C) ≤ liminf_i M_O(S_{φ(i)}). ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce to one admissible form ω for C in O, since M_O(C) is a supremum.
tsupport ω is compact, so by (1) and φ(i) → ∞ it lies in U_{φ(i)} for all large i; there ω is admissible for S_{φ(i)} in O and ofReal(currentEval(S_{φ(i)}, ω)) ≤ M_O(S_{φ(i)}).
By (2) along φ, ofReal(currentEval(S_{φ(i)}, ω)) → ofReal(C(ω)); pass to the liminf and take the supremum over ω.

subproblems.title: Upper bound on compact sets from sub-subsequence comparisons on thin neighbourhoods (Simon 7.2.4 (13))
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let μ and μ_j (j ∈ ℕ) be measures on the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^P (evaluated on arbitrary sets as outer measures, values in [0, ∞]). Assume (a) μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, and (s) for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, every ε > 0 and every strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ there are a set W with K ⊆ W ⊆ thickening(ε, K) = {x : inf_{y∈K} |x − y| < ε} and a strictly increasing φ' : ℕ → ℕ with limsup_{i→∞} μ_{ψ(φ'(i))}(W) ≤ μ(W). Then limsup_{j→∞} μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P (lim sup in [0, ∞]).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μs : ℕ → Measure (Euclid P)) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → μ K < ∞) → (∀ (K : Set (Euclid P)) (ε : ℝ), IsCompact K → 0 < ε → ∀ ψ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono ψ → ∃ W : Set (Euclid P), K ⊆ W ∧ W ⊆ thickening ε K ∧ ∃ φ' : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ' ∧ limsup (fun i => μs (ψ (φ' i)) W) atTop ≤ μ W) → ∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → limsup (fun j => μs j K) atTop ≤ μ K
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 7.2.4, (13) and the remark after it (chapter-07.txt lines 264–280: limsup μ_{T_j}(K) ≤ M_{dist(·,K)<ε}(T), then ε ↓ 0; "we can repeat the argument for a subsequence of any given subsequence, hence it holds for the original sequence"). This is the measure-theoretic core of step 3(b) of the parent proof.
1. Fix a compact K ⊆ ℝ^P and put ℓ := limsup_j μ_j(K) ∈ [0, ∞]. Claim: ℓ ≤ μ(thickening(ε, K)) for every ε > 0.
2. Suppose the claim fails for some ε > 0, i.e. μ(thickening(ε, K)) < ℓ. Since [0, ∞] is densely ordered, choose b with μ(thickening(ε, K)) < b < ℓ.
3. Since b < limsup_j μ_j(K), the inequality μ_j(K) > b holds for infinitely many j (otherwise μ_j(K) ≤ b for all large j, which would force ℓ ≤ b). Listing these j in increasing order gives a strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ with μ_{ψ(i)}(K) > b for every i (Mathlib extraction_of_frequently_atTop).
4. Apply (s) to K, ε and ψ: there are W with K ⊆ W ⊆ thickening(ε, K) and a strictly increasing φ' with limsup_i μ_{ψ(φ'(i))}(W) ≤ μ(W).
5. For every i, μ_{ψ(φ'(i))}(W) ≥ μ_{ψ(φ'(i))}(K) > b, by monotonicity of the measure μ_{ψ(φ'(i))} (K ⊆ W) and step 3 applied at the index φ'(i). A sequence that is ≥ b at every index has lim sup ≥ b, so b ≤ limsup_i μ_{ψ(φ'(i))}(W).
6. Hence b ≤ limsup_i μ_{ψ(φ'(i))}(W) ≤ μ(W) ≤ μ(thickening(ε, K)) < b, using step 4 and monotonicity of μ (W ⊆ thickening(ε, K)); this contradiction proves the claim.
7. K is compact, hence closed. The set cthickening(1, K) = {x : dist(x, K) ≤ 1} is closed and bounded in ℝ^P, hence compact, so by (a), μ(thickening(1, K)) ≤ μ(cthickening(1, K)) < ∞. For a closed set K with μ(thickening(R, K)) < ∞ for some R > 0, continuity of measure from above along the decreasing sets thickening(r, K), whose intersection over r > 0 is closure(K) = K, gives μ(thickening(r, K)) → μ(K) as r ↓ 0 (Mathlib tendsto_measure_thickening_of_isClosed).
8. By the claim, ℓ ≤ μ(thickening(r, K)) for every r > 0; letting r ↓ 0 and using step 7 yields ℓ = limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K). ∎
proof_key_steps: For fixed ε > 0, if limsup_j μ_j(K) > b > μ(thickening(ε, K)), extract a strictly increasing ψ with μ_{ψ(i)}(K) > b for all i.
Hypothesis (s) gives W ⊇ K inside thickening(ε, K) and φ' with limsup_i μ_{ψ(φ'(i))}(W) ≤ μ(W) ≤ μ(thickening(ε, K)) < b, whereas μ_{ψ(φ'(i))}(W) ≥ μ_{ψ(φ'(i))}(K) > b for all i: contradiction.
Let ε ↓ 0: μ(thickening(ε, K)) → μ(K) since K is closed and μ(thickening(1, K)) ≤ μ(cthickening(1, K)) < ∞ by (a).

subproblems.title: The weak limit is minimizing in ℝ^P (Simon 7.2.4 (8))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. For j ∈ ℕ let U_j ⊆ ℝ^P be any sets and S_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U_j), and let C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) be integer multiplicity. Assume (1) for every r ∈ ℝ, closedBall(0, r) ⊆ U_j for all sufficiently large j; (2) S_j ⇀ C in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly); (3) (local comparison) for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, every ε > 0 and every strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ there are an open W with K ⊆ W ⊆ thickening(ε, K) and a strictly increasing φ' : ℕ → ℕ such that limsup_i M_W(S_{ψ(φ'(i))}) ≤ M_W(S) for every integer multiplicity S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with SameBoundary S C (∂S = ∂C if n ≥ 1, vacuous if n = 0) and spt(S − C) ⊆ K. Then C is minimizing in ℝ^P (IsMinimizingIn C univ): C is integer multiplicity, and M_W(C) ≤ M_W(S) whenever W ⊆ ℝ^P is open with closure W compact (CompactlyContained W ℝ^P), S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) is integer multiplicity, SameBoundary S C, spt(S − C) is compact and spt(S − C) ⊆ ℝ^P ∩ W. Notation: 𝒟_n(V) = GeometricCurrentOn V n; 𝒟ⁿ(V) = TestFormOn V n (smooth compactly supported n-forms ω on ℝ^P with tsupport ω ⊆ V); for Y ∈ 𝒟_n(V) and any O ⊆ ℝ^P, M_O(Y) := Y.massOn O = sup{ofReal(Y(ω)) : ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V), tsupport ω ⊆ O, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x} ∈ [0, ∞] (SimonGMT massOn, |·| the Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors); currentEval(Y, ω) := Y(ω) if ω is a test form with tsupport ω ⊆ V and 0 otherwise; S_j ⇀ C (ConvergesWeakly Ss C) means currentEval(S_j, ω) → C(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P); thickening(ε, K) = {x : inf_{y∈K} |x − y| < ε}.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Us : ℕ → Set (Euclid P)) (Ss : (j : ℕ) → GeometricCurrentOn (Us j) n) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), (∀ R : ℝ, ∀ᶠ j in atTop, closedBall (0 : Euclid P) R ⊆ Us j) → IsIntegerMultiplicity C → ConvergesWeakly Ss C → (∀ (K : Set (Euclid P)) (ε : ℝ), IsCompact K → 0 < ε → ∀ ψ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono ψ → ∃ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W ∧ K ⊆ W ∧ W ⊆ thickening ε K ∧ ∃ φ' : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ' ∧ ∀ S : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, IsIntegerMultiplicity S → SameBoundary S C → (S - C).support ⊆ K → limsup (fun j => (Ss (ψ (φ' j))).massOn W) atTop ≤ S.massOn W) → IsMinimizingIn C univ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 7.2.4 (8)–(12) and the lower-semicontinuity step after (12) (chapter-07.txt lines 222–263); step 1 of the parent proof. Siblings used: mass_lsc (M_O(C) ≤ liminf_i M_O(S_{φ(i)}) for every set O and strictly increasing φ, under (1), (2)) and minimality_localizes (accepted cmc_massOn_le_of_le_near_support: if U ⊆ ℝ^P is open, S, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) are integer multiplicity, K is compact with spt(S − T) ⊆ K, W ⊆ W' are open with K ⊆ W, closure W' compact and contained in U, and M_W(T) ≤ M_W(S), then M_{W'}(T) ≤ M_{W'}(S)). The latter packages exactly the locality argument (L4) and the additivity computation M_W(C) = μ_C(W') + μ_C(W ∖ W') ≤ … of parent step 1.
1. The first component of IsMinimizingIn C ℝ^P, that C is integer multiplicity, is a hypothesis.
2. Let W ⊆ ℝ^P be open with closure W compact (and closure W ⊆ ℝ^P), let S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) be integer multiplicity with SameBoundary S C, and suppose K := spt(S − C) is compact with K ⊆ ℝ^P ∩ W, so K ⊆ W. We must show M_W(C) ≤ M_W(S).
3. Since K is compact, W is open and K ⊆ W, there is ε > 0 with thickening(ε, K) ⊆ W (a compact subset of an open set has a uniform metric neighbourhood inside it; Mathlib IsCompact.exists_thickening_subset_open).
4. Apply hypothesis (3) to K, ε and the strictly increasing map ψ := id. It yields an open W' with K ⊆ W' ⊆ thickening(ε, K) and a strictly increasing φ' such that limsup_i M_{W'}(S_{φ'(i)}) ≤ M_{W'}(S') for every admissible competitor S'. The current S is admissible: it is integer multiplicity, SameBoundary S C holds, and spt(S − C) = K ⊆ K. Hence limsup_i M_{W'}(S_{φ'(i)}) ≤ M_{W'}(S).
5. The sibling mass_lsc, applied with φ := φ' and O := W' (its hypotheses are (1) and (2)), gives M_{W'}(C) ≤ liminf_i M_{W'}(S_{φ'(i)}). For every sequence in [0, ∞], liminf ≤ limsup along atTop. Therefore M_{W'}(C) ≤ liminf_i M_{W'}(S_{φ'(i)}) ≤ limsup_i M_{W'}(S_{φ'(i)}) ≤ M_{W'}(S).
6. Apply the sibling minimality_localizes (cmc_massOn_le_of_le_near_support, whose frozen statement names the smaller open set W and the larger one W') with the instantiation (U, S, T, K, W, W') := (ℝ^P, S, C, K, W', W), where W' is the open set from step 4 and W the given open set: ℝ^P is open; S and C are integer multiplicity; K is compact and spt(S − C) ⊆ K; W' and W are open; K ⊆ W' by step 4; W' ⊆ thickening(ε, K) ⊆ W by steps 3–4; closure W is compact and contained in ℝ^P (CompactlyContained W ℝ^P); and M_{W'}(C) ≤ M_{W'}(S) by step 5. Its conclusion is M_W(C) ≤ M_W(S).
7. Since W and S were arbitrary, C is minimizing in ℝ^P. ∎
proof_key_steps: Given an admissible pair (W, S), K := spt(S − C) ⊆ W is compact; choose ε > 0 with thickening(ε, K) ⊆ W.

Hypothesis (3) with ψ = id and the competitor S gives an open W' ⊇ K inside thickening(ε, K) and φ' with limsup_i M_{W'}(S_{φ'(i)}) ≤ M_{W'}(S); mass_lsc and liminf ≤ limsup give M_{W'}(C) ≤ M_{W'}(S).
minimality_localizes transfers M_{W'}(C) ≤ M_{W'}(S) from W' to W.

subproblems.title: Semicontinuity of the mass measures along the sequence: finiteness and lim sup bound on compacts, lim inf bound on open sets (Simon 7.2.4 (13), (14))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. For j ∈ ℕ let U_j ⊆ ℝ^P be open and S_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U_j), and let C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P). Assume (1) for every r ∈ ℝ, closedBall(0, r) ⊆ U_j for all sufficiently large j; (2) S_j ⇀ C in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly); (3) (local comparison) for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, every ε > 0 and every strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ there are an open W with K ⊆ W ⊆ thickening(ε, K) and a strictly increasing φ' : ℕ → ℕ such that limsup_i M_W(S_{ψ(φ'(i))}) ≤ M_W(S) for every integer multiplicity S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with SameBoundary S C (∂S = ∂C if n ≥ 1, vacuous if n = 0) and spt(S − C) ⊆ K. Let R_j be an integer multiplicity representation of S_j in U_j for every j (R_j : IMRep U_j n with R_j.Represents S_j) and R an integer multiplicity representation of C in ℝ^P; put μ_j := R_j.measure = θ_j Hⁿ⌞M_j and μ := R.measure = θ Hⁿ⌞M. Then (a) μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P; (b) limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P; (c) μ(G) ≤ liminf_j μ_j(G) for every open G ⊆ ℝ^P (lim sup and lim inf in [0, ∞]). Notation: 𝒟_n(V) = GeometricCurrentOn V n; 𝒟ⁿ(V) = TestFormOn V n (smooth compactly supported n-forms ω on ℝ^P with tsupport ω ⊆ V); for Y ∈ 𝒟_n(V) and any O ⊆ ℝ^P, M_O(Y) := Y.massOn O = sup{ofReal(Y(ω)) : ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V), tsupport ω ⊆ O, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x} ∈ [0, ∞] (SimonGMT massOn, |·| the Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors); currentEval(Y, ω) := Y(ω) if ω is a test form with tsupport ω ⊆ V and 0 otherwise; S_j ⇀ C (ConvergesWeakly Ss C) means currentEval(S_j, ω) → C(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P); thickening(ε, K) = {x : inf_{y∈K} |x − y| < ε}.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Us : ℕ → Set (Euclid P)) (Ss : (j : ℕ) → GeometricCurrentOn (Us j) n) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), (∀ j, IsOpen (Us j)) → (∀ R : ℝ, ∀ᶠ j in atTop, closedBall (0 : Euclid P) R ⊆ Us j) → ConvergesWeakly Ss C → (∀ (K : Set (Euclid P)) (ε : ℝ), IsCompact K → 0 < ε → ∀ ψ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono ψ → ∃ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W ∧ K ⊆ W ∧ W ⊆ thickening ε K ∧ ∃ φ' : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ' ∧ ∀ S : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, IsIntegerMultiplicity S → SameBoundary S C → (S - C).support ⊆ K → limsup (fun j => (Ss (ψ (φ' j))).massOn W) atTop ≤ S.massOn W) → ∀ Rs : (j : ℕ) → IMRep (Us j) n, (∀ j, (Rs j).Represents (Ss j)) → ∀ R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, R.Represents C → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → R.measure K < ∞) ∧ (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → limsup (fun j => (Rs j).measure K) atTop ≤ R.measure K) ∧ (∀ G : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen G → R.measure G ≤ liminf (fun j => (Rs j).measure G) atTop)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 7.2.4 (13), (14) (chapter-07.txt lines 264–284); steps 3(a)–(c) of the parent proof. Statement (c) is proved for every open G (the parent needs it only for bounded G) because the sibling mass_lsc holds for every set. Siblings used: mass_equals_rep_measure (accepted cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure: if U ⊆ ℝ^P is open and R represents T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), then M_W(T) = R.measure(W) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P), mass_lsc and limsup_criterion.
1. (Masses on open sets are weights.) ℝ^P is open and R represents C, so M_G(C) = μ(G) for every open G ⊆ ℝ^P; for each j, U_j is open and R_j represents S_j, so M_G(S_j) = μ_j(G) for every open G ⊆ ℝ^P (mass_equals_rep_measure).
2. (a) Let K ⊆ ℝ^P be compact. K is closed, hence Borel, so by the definition of a measure with density and of restriction, μ(K) = ∫_K θ d(Hⁿ⌞M) = ∫_{K∩M} θ dHⁿ = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ. Since K is compact and K ⊆ ℝ^P, the field locallyIntegrable_mult of R gives ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ ≠ ∞. Hence μ(K) < ∞.
3. (C is an admissible competitor for itself.) C is integer multiplicity, witnessed by R. SameBoundary C C holds: for n = 0 it is True by definition, and for n = m + 1 it is the equality ∂C = ∂C. Moreover spt(C − C) = ∅: by definition spt(C − C) = ℝ^P ∖ Z, where Z is the union of the open sets V with closure V compact and contained in ℝ^P on which C − C vanishes; for x ∈ ℝ^P the ball B(x, 1) is open, its closure lies in the compact closed ball closedBall(x, 1) and is therefore compact, and C − C vanishes on it because (C − C)(ω) = C(ω) − C(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P); so x ∈ Z. In particular spt(C − C) ⊆ K for every set K.
4. (b) Apply the sibling limsup_criterion to the measures μ_j and μ. Its hypothesis (a) is step 2. For its hypothesis (s), let K be compact, ε > 0 and ψ strictly increasing. Hypothesis (3) applied to K, ε, ψ gives an open W with K ⊆ W ⊆ thickening(ε, K) and a strictly increasing φ' such that limsup_i M_W(S_{ψ(φ'(i))}) ≤ M_W(S) for every admissible S; by step 3 we may take S := C, which gives limsup_i M_W(S_{ψ(φ'(i))}) ≤ M_W(C). Since W is open, step 1 rewrites every term: M_W(S_{ψ(φ'(i))}) = μ_{ψ(φ'(i))}(W) for every i, and M_W(C) = μ(W). Hence limsup_i μ_{ψ(φ'(i))}(W) ≤ μ(W), so W and φ' witness (s). The conclusion of limsup_criterion is exactly (b).
5. (c) Let G ⊆ ℝ^P be open. The sibling mass_lsc with φ := id and O := G (its hypotheses are (1) and (2)) gives M_G(C) ≤ liminf_j M_G(S_j). By step 1, M_G(C) = μ(G) and M_G(S_j) = μ_j(G) for every j, so μ(G) ≤ liminf_j μ_j(G). ∎
proof_key_steps: Masses on open sets equal the weights of the representations (mass_equals_rep_measure).
(a): μ(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by local integrability of the multiplicity of R.
(b): C is an admissible competitor for itself (integer multiplicity via R, SameBoundary C C, spt(C − C) = ∅); hypothesis (3) with S = C, rewritten into weights, is hypothesis (s) of limsup_criterion.
(c): mass_lsc with φ = id, rewritten into weights.
